      <title>The House of Slaughter — How a Brother's Trap Nearly Destroyed the Greatest Hindu Empire</title>
      <description>In 1443, the brother of King Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara orchestrated one of medieval India's most chilling assassinations — luring the empire's nobles one by one into a newly built house where assassins butchered them behind a wall of deafening drums, then attacking the king himself with a hidden dagger. Deva Raya survived by fighting back with his own throne and escaping through the harem, but the massacre gutted the empire's leadership, and the ensuing war with the Bahmani Sultan Ala-ud-din cost the king his eldest son and forced him into a humiliating tribute agreement. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900), drawing on the accounts of Abdur Razzak and Firishtah.</description>
